name: list_tasks
title: List tasks
description: List tasks with optional filters — the same listing as `vibeflow tasks` (same filters, same scope, same order). Unfiltered: ROOT tasks only (a child belongs to its parent's card — set children:true to include them). Filtered (status/type/user/tag/search): an explicit search returning EVERY match, children included. `search` is a fuzzy relevance search over title, description, comments and tags (same shared matcher as `vibeflow tasks --search`, ranked by score then id, named in the `order` echo). Counts are labelled by scope: totalMatching (every match), totalRoots (matching roots), hiddenChildren (matches omitted by root-only scope), returned (rows in `tasks`), limit (echoed RESOLVED — 0 is not supported and falls back to the default of 20, named in `limitNotice`; there is no unbounded mode, page with nextCursor or CLI --all for everything), truncated + hint (present only when the limit cut rows). Position: offset (0-based index of the first returned row), remaining (rows in THIS query's scope NOT in this response — totalRoots-based when root-only, totalMatching-based otherwise, so offset + returned + remaining always equals the scope size; 0 means exhausted), nextCursor (opaque continuation, null exactly when exhausted), order (the effective sort applied, so a continuation is stable). Projected rows (fields) always carry commentCount/fileCount even when the arrays are omitted. Use it to browse or search the board; use get_task when you already hold an id, and claim_next_task when you want the next unit of work claimed rather than just listed.

name: get_task
title: Get task
description: Get a single task by ID with full details including comments and files. Pass `fields` (e.g. ["id","title","status"]) for a compact projection instead of the full record. Read-only; changes nothing. Use it when list_tasks gave you an id or you already hold one; use list_tasks to search the board, and claim_next_task to pull the next unit of work.

name: get_project
title: Get project
description: Return the resolved project this server is attached to: name, absolute root, git branch and mode. Read-only; takes no input and changes nothing. Call it when you need board location or branch context before operating on tasks.

name: create_task
title: Create task
description: Create a new task with title, description, and metadata. Pass `fields` (e.g. ["id","title","status"]) for a compact answer instead of the full task object; pass dryRun to validate without writing anything. LINKS merge: `links` ADDS every listed taskId+type pair to the new task and `parent` (when given) is folded into the same union, so sending both merges once and a pair named twice is a no-op — the same MERGE semantic update_task has, where a link you do not name is simply absent (a new task has nothing to preserve). `links: []` is REFUSED — omit the field for no links. Use it for a new unit of work; use update_task to change an existing task, and add_comment to discuss one without editing it.

name: update_task
title: Update task
description:
Update an existing task. Supports status changes, title/description updates, adding comments, and changing the task's links (parent/relates/blocks). Pass `fields` (e.g. ["id","status"]) for a compact answer instead of the full task object; pass dryRun to preview the edit without writing anything, and `branch` to record the work branch (required on the review transition when the project sets createBranch). REVIEW GATE (same rules as `vibeflow tasks --edit`, same codes): status "review" REQUIRES `comment` (refused REVIEW_COMMENT_REQUIRED); an ANNOTATED task (url + selector) additionally REQUIRES a verdict (`setVerify` pass/fail/cannot — refused VERIFY_REQUIRED); `commitMessage` is REQUIRED when auto-commit is ON (refused COMMIT_MESSAGE_REQUIRED); a Research task must NOT carry a verdict (refused RESEARCH_VERIFY_NOT_ALLOWED — submit Research with its .md report, no verdict). Pass setVerify to record your verification verdict: "pass" attests the task IS implemented correctly (verified=true, green badge — required for annotated tasks at the review transition, which `vibeflow verify` never sets itself), "fail" records that it is NOT implemented correctly (verified=false, amber badge, the review gate rejects it), and "cannot" clears the verdict back to absent (no badge) for a task that cannot be assessed here — "cannot" REQUIRES verifyReason, which is recorded in the task's activity. Use it to change a task you already hold; use add_comment to discuss without changing fields, and verify_task to actually RUN visual verification (a verdict here records an assessment, it runs nothing).

LINKS — everything merges, and `clearLinks` is the only destructive path. `links` and `addLinks` both MERGE: a link you do not name is PRESERVED, and re-sending a link that is already there is a no-op, so neither of them can destroy a link by being incomplete. `removeLinks` removes exactly the taskId+type pairs you name and leaves every other link alone. `clearLinks: true` is the ONLY way to remove links wholesale — to drop a single link, name that taskId+type in `removeLinks` rather than editing `links`. Omitting all four fields leaves links untouched. The CLI's `--set-parent`/`--relates`/`--blocks`/`--unrelates`/`--unblocks` behave the same way (each is surgical and preserves every link it does not name), so the CLI and MCP surfaces now agree on link semantics.

name: claim_next_task
title: Claim next task
description: Claim the highest-priority todo task and set it to in-progress: the returned object IS the claimed task. Roots first: a todo ROOT is claimed before any child — the root is the unit of work, so work through its children after claiming it. When no todo root is claimable, falls back to the highest-priority matching todo child of live work (parent chain todo/in-progress/review) and says so explicitly (a CHILD_CLAIM notice naming the parent); children of backlog/done parents are refused, never sliced off. Optional type/user/tag filters narrow the pool (tags every-match); pass dryRun to preview the claim without moving the task. An empty board — or a valid filter matching nothing — is a SUCCESS with a `null` result, the same as 'vibeflow tasks --next --json' reporting `task:null` with exit 0. Use it to pull the next unit of work; use list_tasks to browse without claiming, and get_task to inspect a task you already hold.

name: add_comment
title: Add comment
description: Add a comment to a task without changing any of its fields. The body is `comment` — the same name as the CLI's --comment flag and update_task's field. `author` defaults to agent; pass dryRun to validate without writing. Use it to discuss or record progress; use update_task's `comment` when the note accompanies a status or field change (review REQUIRES the note on the same call).

name: attach_file
title: Attach file
description: Attach a file to a task (content as base64) without changing any of its fields. Re-attaching an existing filename overwrites its bytes in place — the file list gains no duplicate. Pass dryRun to validate without writing. A filename ending in `.md` is what satisfies the research-report gate: a `type:"Research"` task is refused review with RESEARCH_REPORT_REQUIRED until a `.md` is attached, so attaching the report is how to recover from that refusal. Use it for reports, screenshots and evidence; use add_comment for discussion text.

name: get_file
title: Get file
description: Download a file attached to a task, returned as base64 with its filename, content type and size. Give the task `id` plus the attached `filename` (either mode) or the online `fileId` (remote mode only). Read-only; changes nothing. Use it to read back an attachment the file list only names — the remote list carries no bytes, so this is how an agent actually sees the content.

name: pull
title: Pull board
description: Pull the online board into the local task store: the inverse of a push. ADDITIVE and never destructive — tasks and files the board holds are added or merged field-by-field into `.vibeflow/`, local-only data is never dropped, and nothing is ever deleted. On a conflicting field the LOCAL value wins by default, except `status`, which follows the remote record (the board is truth for workflow state) unless preferLocal restores local-wins for it; pass preferRemote to let the remote value win on every conflicting field instead. A second pull of an unchanged board is a byte-no-op (unchanged tasks are not rewritten, identical files untouched). Pass dryRun to preview the pull without writing anything. Use it to bring a board's tasks and file bytes local after working in another checkout or on the web; use list_tasks to browse without writing, and push to send local work up.

name: verify_task
title: Verify task
description: Run visual verification on a task with the Playwright engine: it loads the task's annotated page (url + selector) and compares the live element against the baseline captured at annotation time. MUTATES: every run appends a system comment with the outcome — pass dryRun to resolve the id and preview without launching a browser or writing anything. Pass `url` to check a different app URL for this run only, and `timeoutMs` (default 60000, refused VERIFY_TIMEOUT past it) for slow apps. A task with no baseline refuses with E_NO_BASELINE (re-annotate in `vibeflow kanban` to capture one); an unknown id with E_NOT_FOUND. Use it to check an annotated task before review; use update_task's setVerify to record the human verdict (this tool never sets it).

name: start_kanban
title: Start kanban server
description: Start the local kanban board server and return the instruction block the CLI prints: the kanban URL, the localhost URL when bound to 0.0.0.0, the agent prompt, and the overlay integration guide. IDEMPOTENT — one server per process; a second call returns the running instance (alreadyRunning:true) instead of fighting for the port. Pass dryRun to report the URLs without binding anything. Call it once before get_integration_guide so the guide carries real URLs; skip it entirely for remote or Docker setups where a localhost server is unreachable.

name: get_integration_guide
title: Get integration guide
description: Get the overlay/bookmarklet integration instructions — the text of the /inject page: the script tag to paste, the browser-console snippet, the bookmarklet, and the /inject URL. Works whether or not the server is running; when it is not, the guide is built against the default port and the result says serverRunning:false, so call start_kanban first for real URLs.
